title: Card pool definition
description: The set of cards legally available to players at a format's snapshot date. Two representations are supported: an intensional rule (release cutoff, resolved against the releases dataset at build time) and an extensional list (explicit passcodes, typically imported from a vetted external definition). A pool may carry both; the validator cross-checks them against each other where possible.

variant_passcodes.description: Additional artwork-variant passcodes of this card that were also legal in period (cdb alias within +/-10 of the base code). Recorded explicitly so generated whitelists can reproduce reference lists code-for-code.

cards.description: extensional: the full explicit pool, one entry per canonical card. Must be present when kind=extensional.

cutoff.description: release-cutoff: every card with a release event dated <= cutoff_date in one of the scoped territories (per data/releases/products/) is in the pool, then include/exclude exceptions apply. Must be present when kind=release-cutoff. Once releases coverage exists, `python -m retroformats materialize` writes the derived pool into `cards`; the validator recomputes it from release data on every run and fails on drift, so the committed list stays a reviewable projection of the release facts.

territories.description: Which territories' release events count toward availability. Defaults to every TCG territory when the pool region is TCG (historically, a card released anywhere in the TCG was tournament-legal TCG-wide - e.g. Europe-only Retro Pack cards at a US event). Narrow this for pools that genuinely track one territory's availability.

product.description: Product id (data/releases/products/<id>.json) whose release events do not count toward this pool. Cards remain if available through another product.

exclude_products.description: Product-level availability exceptions - e.g. a format defined against one territory's street date (The Shining Darkness's European release preceding the NA-anchored cutoff), or product classes the format's definition omits (Duel Terminal machines).

from.description: The passcode release derivation naturally resolves the printing to.

to.description: The BabelCDB sibling passcode correctly scoped (cdb `ot`) for this pool's region, used in the materialized pool instead.

region_substitutions.description: Cards whose release-derived canonical passcode is scoped (BabelCDB `ot`) for the wrong region for this pool - a code an EDOPro official-cards room in this region would reject. Substitutes the correctly-scoped sibling passcode BabelCDB ships for the same printing. Applied at materialize time (retroformats/releases.py); the banlist's own passcode is deliberately left untouched and bridged back to at lflist-build time (retroformats/lflist.py) rather than requiring banlist data to be rewritten.

legality_basis.description: What this pool CLAIMS to be. Release events record physical availability; a pool is a LEGALITY POLICY over them, and the two are distinct concepts. availability: the pure derivation - every card physically obtainable in the scoped territories by the cutoff, no tournament-policy claim. historical-policy: reconstructs what period tournament policy actually permitted at a specific time/jurisdiction (requires period policy evidence for its exceptions). community-retrospective: follows the modern community's convention for a retrospectively-defined format (sourced to the community's own references); may deliberately differ from what was registerable at the historical event the format is named for.
